activities.anchor: Writing during the English Civil War
activities.caption: rebuild Hobbes's geometric proof, premise by premise
activities.name: polHobbesOrder

config.prompt: Hobbes built the argument like a geometric proof. Assemble it:
items: Premise one: humans are roughly equal in vulnerability — the weakest can kill the strongest, by stealth or alliance
Premise two: resources are scarce and we are competitive, so we anticipate attack and strike first
Conclusion: without a common power to overawe everyone, life is a war of all against all
The agreement: authorise an absolute sovereign, because any weaker arrangement reopens the war
config.why: Each step leans on the one before it — which is why objections to the argument must attack the premises, not the archaeology.

activities.anchor: Hobbes was describing how humans actually lived before
activities.caption: find the faulty line in this student's gloss on Hobbes
activities.name: polHobbesSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's gloss on Hobbes is wrong — click it:
lines: Writing in the English Civil War, Hobbes builds the argument like a geometric proof.
Premise: humans are roughly equal in vulnerability, and scarcity makes them strike first.
Without a common power, life is 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — a war of all against all.
Hobbes grounds the state on divine right and tradition, like the theorists before him.
The state of nature is a thought experiment, not an anthropology — no one ever had to live it.
config.correction: The reverse — Hobbes founds the state on self-interest rationally calculated: the first fully secular theory of political obligation.
config.why: Divine right and tradition are exactly what Hobbes abandons; even his opponents go on arguing on his terrain.

activities.anchor: accepts Hobbes's method and rejects his anthropology
activities.caption: pair each Lockean term with its work
activities.name: polLockeMatch

config.prompt: Locke keeps the method and swaps the anthropology — pair the pieces:

pairs.right: discovered by reason — forbids harming anyone in life, health, liberty or possessions
you own yourself and the fruits of mixing your labour with the world

pairs.left: the inconvenience of the state of nature
pairs.right: not violence but bias — everyone judges their own case
rulers become predators — rebellion is then a duty, not merely permitted

config.why: Rights precede government: the state is a limited, conditional security service — the argument copied nearly verbatim into the Declaration of Independence.

activities.anchor: means a free-for-all with no rules
activities.caption: true or false — inside Locke's state of nature
activities.name: polLockeJudge

statements.s: Locke's state of nature has no rules at all.
statements.why: It already has law — natural law, discoverable by reason — and even property.

statements.s: What the state of nature lacks is a neutral judge and a reliable enforcer.
statements.why: That defect — bias, everyone judging their own case — is the specific job government is created for.

statements.s: For Locke, government is the source of your rights.
statements.why: The state is the security service for rights you had all along; modern 'rights exist prior to government' talk descends from this.

statements.s: When rulers become predators, the contract is void and rebellion is a duty.
statements.why: Authority is limited and conditional — the intellectual ammunition of 1688 and 1776 alike.

activities.anchor: opens with the tradition's most famous sentence
activities.caption: file each claim under its contract thinker
activities.name: polThinkerSort

config.prompt: Three answers to one question — file each claim under its thinker:

items.label: any weaker arrangement reopens the war — so authorise an absolute sovereign
life without a common power is a war of all against all
the state is the security service for rights you had all along
everyone judges their own case — government exists for impartial enforcement
when rulers become predators, the contract is void and rebellion is a duty
each citizen gives themselves wholly to the community and shares lawmaking through the general will
the first person who fenced land and said 'this is mine' founded modern misery

config.why: Same method — reason from a hypothetical agreement — three different anthropologies; the disagreement decides everything downstream.

activities.anchor: are partly an attempt to keep Rousseau's democratic insight
activities.caption: walk the 'forced to be free' danger
activities.name: polWillBranch

config.root: The general will is real but interpretive. Walk the danger Rousseau's own phrase exposes.

start.text: A state claims to interpret the general will. What does that claim license, on Rousseau's own phrase?

choices.label: Dissenters may be coerced 'for their own freedom'
Nothing — no one may ever interpret for the people

interpret.text: That is the 'forced to be free' move: whoever claims to interpret the general will claims unlimited power — the danger visible in Rousseau's own writing.

choices.label: How did the twentieth century make this lethal?

lethal.text: The people's democracies made the ambiguity lethal: an interpreter speaking for 'the people' answered to nobody.

repair.text: Rawls keeps the democratic insight but removes the interpreter's blank cheque: the agreement is proceduralised behind a veil of ignorance, not entrusted to whoever speaks for the people.

config.why: Majorities can be wrong about the general will — and an unaccountable interpreter turns popular sovereignty into its opposite.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — Mill's boundary for the state
activities.name: polMillCloze

config.text: The only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over any member of a civilized community, against his will, is to prevent %%0%% to others. Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is %%1%%. Mill called the majority's temptation to legislate its own tastes 'the tyranny of the %%2%%'.
config.hint: Three single words: what coercion may prevent; the individual's standing over his own body and mind; the phrase Mill used for majority rule.

activities.anchor: rational caution protects the position you might occupy
activities.caption: drag the divider — what the difference principle permits vs forbids
activities.name: polDiffCompare

config.prompt: One principle, two verdicts — drag to compare what the difference principle allows and blocks:

before.label: permits
before.text: The surgeon out-earning the cleaner: higher pay recruits talent that then improves everyone's healthcare. Inequality attached to offices open to all under fair opportunity — and it lifts the least advantaged.

after.label: forbids
after.text: Inequalities that merely reflect inherited position, or that leave the worst off where they were — no recruitment argument, no gain for the least advantaged, no pass.

config.why: Rawls explicitly permits inequality — what the principle demands is a filter: it passes only when it benefits the least advantaged.
